pattern: あげる / くれる / もらう
meaning: give (to someone else); give (to me or my group); receive
structure: Noun (receiver) + に + Noun + を + あげる / Noun (giver) + が + Noun + を + くれる / Noun (giver) + に + Noun + を + もらう
usage: くれる is used only when the receiver is the speaker or someone in the speaker's group. With もらう the giver can be marked with に or から.

examples.japanese: 私は弟に古いゲームをあげた。
examples.english: I gave my old game to my little brother.

examples.japanese: 姉が誕生日にかわいいかばんをくれました。
examples.english: My older sister gave me a cute bag for my birthday.

examples.japanese: 友達から旅行のおみやげをもらった。
examples.english: I got a souvenir from my friend's trip.

meaning: do something for someone (as a favor)
structure: Verb-te + あげる
usage: Said directly to a superior it can sound condescending; use the humble お〜しましょうか (お持ちしましょうか) instead.

examples.japanese: 妹の宿題を手伝ってあげました。
examples.english: I helped my little sister with her homework.

examples.japanese: 道に迷っている人に、駅までの行き方を教えてあげた。
examples.english: I showed someone who was lost how to get to the station.

examples.japanese: 重そうだね。持ってあげようか。
examples.english: That looks heavy. Want me to carry it for you?

meaning: someone does something for me (or my group)
structure: Verb-te + くれる
usage: The subject is the person doing the favor; the one who benefits is the speaker or someone close to them.

examples.japanese: 友達が引っ越しを手伝ってくれた。
examples.english: A friend helped me move.

examples.japanese: 父が駅まで車で送ってくれました。
examples.english: My father drove me to the station.

examples.japanese: 母が毎朝お弁当を作ってくれます。
examples.english: My mother makes me a boxed lunch every morning.

meaning: have someone do something (for me); get someone to do
structure: Verb-te + もらう
usage: The receiver of the favor is the subject, and the person who does the action is marked with に.

examples.japanese: 先輩にレポートを見てもらった。
examples.english: I had a senior student look over my report.

examples.japanese: 友達に写真を撮ってもらった。
examples.english: I had a friend take my picture.

examples.japanese: 分からないところを先生に説明してもらいました。
examples.english: I had the teacher explain the parts I didn't understand.

meaning: (honorific) someone kindly does for me; (humble) I receive the favor of someone doing
structure: Verb-te + くださる / Verb-te + いただく
usage: くださる is the honorific version of くれる (ます-form: くださいます); いただく is the humble version of もらう.

examples.japanese: 先生が私の作文を直してくださいました。
examples.english: My teacher kindly corrected my essay.

examples.japanese: ホテルの方に、おいしい店を教えていただきました。
examples.english: The hotel staff kindly told me about a good restaurant.

examples.japanese: 今日は来ていただいて、ありがとうございました。
examples.english: Thank you very much for coming today.

meaning: do something and go; go on doing (from now into the future)
structure: Verb-te + いく
usage: Movement or change away from the speaker, or from now toward the future. Compare 〜てくる.

examples.japanese: 雨が降りそうだから、傘を持っていきます。
examples.english: It looks like rain, so I'll take an umbrella.

examples.japanese: これからもっと寒くなっていくでしょう。
examples.english: It will probably keep getting colder from now on.

examples.japanese: 時間があるなら、お茶を飲んでいきませんか。
examples.english: If you have time, won't you have some tea before you go?

meaning: do something and come back; come doing; (change) up to now; start to
structure: Verb-te + くる
usage: Movement or change toward the speaker, or from the past up to now. 行ってきます literally means 'I'll go and come back.'

examples.japanese: ちょっとコンビニに行ってきます。
examples.english: I'm just popping out to the convenience store.

examples.japanese: 日本語が少しずつ分かってきた。
examples.english: I've gradually started to understand Japanese.

examples.japanese: おなかがすいてきた。
examples.english: I'm starting to get hungry.

meaning: finish completely; do by accident; end up doing (with regret)
structure: Verb-te + しまう
usage: In speech 〜てしまう contracts to 〜ちゃう, and 〜でしまう to 〜じゃう (飲んじゃう).

examples.japanese: 電車に傘を忘れてしまいました。
examples.english: I left my umbrella on the train.

examples.japanese: この本はおもしろくて、一晩で読んでしまった。
examples.english: This book was so interesting that I read the whole thing in one night.

examples.japanese: あ、ケーキを全部食べちゃった。
examples.english: Oops, I ate all the cake.

meaning: do in advance (to prepare); do and leave as is
structure: Verb-te + おく
usage: In casual speech 〜ておく often becomes 〜とく (買っとく), and 〜でおく becomes 〜どく (読んどく).

examples.japanese: 旅行の前に、ホテルを予約しておきます。
examples.english: I'll book the hotel before the trip.

examples.japanese: パーティーのために、飲み物を冷やしておいた。
examples.english: I chilled the drinks for the party.

examples.japanese: エアコンはつけておいてください。
examples.english: Please leave the air conditioner on.

meaning: try doing (to see what it is like)
structure: Verb-te + みる
usage: Means trying something out to see the result, not making an effort to do something difficult.

examples.japanese: このシャツ、着てみてもいいですか。
examples.english: May I try this shirt on?

examples.japanese: 新しくできたラーメン屋に行ってみた。
examples.english: I went to check out the new ramen shop.

examples.japanese: 日本の料理を自分で作ってみたいです。
examples.english: I want to try making Japanese food myself.

meaning: has been done (and stays that way); resulting state of a deliberate action
structure: Verb-te + ある
usage: Used with transitive verbs, and the object usually takes が. It implies someone did it on purpose, unlike 〜ている with intransitive verbs (窓が開いている).

examples.japanese: 入り口に地図がはってあります。
examples.english: There's a map put up at the entrance.

examples.japanese: テーブルの上にお皿が並べてあった。
examples.english: Plates had been set out on the table.

examples.japanese: ビールなら冷蔵庫に入れてあるよ。
examples.english: If you want beer, I've put some in the fridge.

meaning: when; at the time when
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj + な / Noun + の + とき
usage: The verb's tense shows the order: 行くとき means before or on the way (the going isn't finished yet); 行ったとき means after arriving. Often written 時 in kanji.

examples.japanese: 子どものとき、よく川で泳ぎました。
examples.english: When I was a child, I often swam in the river.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行くとき、新しいかばんを買いました。
examples.english: I bought a new bag before my trip to Japan.

examples.japanese: 日本へ行ったとき、友達にお土産を買いました。
examples.english: When I went to Japan, I bought souvenirs for my friends there.

meaning: while; during (the whole time); at some point during
structure: Verb-te + いる / Verb-dict / Noun + の + 間（に）
usage: 間 means the action continues through the whole period; 間に means it happens at some point within the period.

examples.japanese: 夏休みの間、祖父の家にいました。
examples.english: I stayed at my grandfather's house during the summer vacation.

examples.japanese: 母が寝ている間に、部屋を掃除した。
examples.english: I cleaned my room while my mother was asleep.

examples.japanese: 電車を待っている間、ずっと本を読んでいた。
examples.english: I read a book the whole time I was waiting for the train.

meaning: looks like; seems; looks about to
structure: Verb-stem / i-Adj stem / na-Adj + そうだ
usage: A judgment from what you see. いい → よさそう, ない → なさそう. Not used with adjectives for plainly visible traits (赤い, かわいい); かわいそう means 'pitiful'.

examples.japanese: そのカレー、辛そうだね。
examples.english: That curry looks spicy.

examples.japanese: 空が暗いですね。雨が降りそうです。
examples.english: The sky is dark. It looks like it's going to rain.

examples.japanese: 久しぶりに会った祖父は元気そうだった。
examples.english: My grandfather, whom I hadn't seen in a while, looked well.

meaning: I heard that; they say that
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + そうだ / na-Adj + だ + そうだ / Noun + だ + そうだ
usage: Attaches to full plain forms, unlike the 'looks like' そうだ, which attaches to stems. It has no past or negative form.

examples.japanese: 天気予報では、明日は雪が降るそうです。
examples.english: The weather forecast says it will snow tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 駅前の本屋は来月なくなるそうだ。
examples.english: I heard the bookstore in front of the station is closing down next month.

examples.japanese: リンさんのお兄さんは医者だそうです。
examples.english: I hear Lin's older brother is a doctor.

meaning: apparently; it seems; I hear
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + らしい
usage: Based on something heard or read, so the speaker sounds a little detached. The 'typical of' らしい (男らしい) is a separate N3 point.

examples.japanese: 駅の近くに新しいカフェができたらしい。
examples.english: Apparently a new café has opened near the station.

examples.japanese: 部屋の電気が消えている。もう寝たらしい。
examples.english: The light in the room is off. Looks like they've already gone to bed.

examples.japanese: あの店のラーメンはとても有名らしいです。
examples.english: Apparently that shop's ramen is really famous.

meaning: it seems; it appears (judging from evidence)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + ようだ / na-Adj + な + ようだ / Noun + の + ようだ
usage: A somewhat formal way to state a judgment from what you observe or feel; みたいだ is the casual equivalent. The 'like, as if' use is covered at N3.

examples.japanese: 誰もいないようですね。
examples.english: It seems nobody's here.

examples.japanese: かぜをひいたようで、朝からのどが痛い。
examples.english: I seem to have caught a cold; my throat has hurt since this morning.

examples.japanese: 外は寒いようだ。みんなコートを着ている。
examples.english: It seems cold outside. Everyone is wearing a coat.

meaning: seems like; looks like; like (casual)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + みたい
usage: Casual equivalent of ようだ. It attaches directly to nouns and na-adjectives (静かみたい) without な or の. Before a noun it becomes みたいな.

examples.japanese: 隣の部屋に誰か来たみたい。
examples.english: Sounds like someone has come to the room next door.

examples.japanese: 今日の彼女は元気がないみたいだね。
examples.english: She doesn't seem very cheerful today, does she?

examples.japanese: このケーキ、お店のケーキみたい！
examples.english: This cake is just like a store-bought one!

meaning: too; too much; excessively
structure: Verb-stem / i-Adj stem / na-Adj + すぎる
usage: Conjugates like a Group 2 verb (すぎた, すぎて). いい → よすぎる, and the adjective ない → なさすぎる.

examples.japanese: ゆうべ飲みすぎて、頭が痛い。
examples.english: I drank too much last night, and now I have a headache.

examples.japanese: この靴は私には大きすぎます。
examples.english: These shoes are too big for me.

examples.japanese: この問題は簡単すぎて、つまらない。
examples.english: This question is too easy, so it's boring.

meaning: how to; way of doing
structure: Verb-stem + 方
usage: The result is a noun, so the object takes の instead of を (日本語の話し方). With する-verbs: 勉強のしかた.

examples.japanese: この機械の使い方を教えてください。
examples.english: Please show me how to use this machine.

examples.japanese: この漢字の読み方が分かりません。
examples.english: I don't know how to read this kanji.

examples.japanese: 祖母においしいみそ汁の作り方を習った。
examples.english: I learned how to make tasty miso soup from my grandmother.

meaning: in the middle of; during (ちゅう); throughout; all over (じゅう)
structure: Noun + 中
usage: ちゅう marks an ongoing activity or a period (会議中, 午前中, 今週中); じゅう means 'throughout' a time or place (一日中, 世界中).

examples.japanese: 父は今、電話中です。
examples.english: My father is on the phone right now.

examples.japanese: 昨日は一日中雨が降っていた。
examples.english: It rained all day yesterday.

examples.japanese: この歌は世界中で知られている。
examples.english: This song is known all over the world.

meaning: intend to; plan to
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + つもり
usage: States a firm personal intention. 〜つもりはない means 'have no intention of'. Asking a superior 〜つもりですか can sound blunt.

examples.japanese: 夏休みは北海道を旅行するつもりです。
examples.english: I intend to travel around Hokkaido during the summer break.

examples.japanese: 今日はお酒を飲まないつもりです。
examples.english: I intend not to drink alcohol today.

examples.japanese: 大学を出たら、どうするつもりですか。
examples.english: What do you plan to do after you graduate from university?

meaning: plan to; be scheduled to
structure: Verb-dict + 予定 / Noun + の + 予定
usage: Refers to a fixed schedule or arrangement, often involving other people; more objective than つもり.

examples.japanese: 来月、大阪に引っ越す予定です。
examples.english: I'm planning to move to Osaka next month.

examples.japanese: 会議は三時に終わる予定です。
examples.english: The meeting is scheduled to end at three.

examples.japanese: 出発は朝八時の予定です。
examples.english: Departure is scheduled for eight in the morning.

meaning: decide to
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことにする
usage: A decision made by the speaker; compare 〜ことになる. 〜ことにしている (N3) means 'make it a rule to'.

examples.japanese: 健康のために、毎朝歩くことにした。
examples.english: I decided to walk every morning for my health.

examples.japanese: 高かったので、買わないことにしました。
examples.english: It was expensive, so I decided not to buy it.

examples.japanese: もう遅いから、タクシーで帰ることにしよう。
examples.english: It's already late, so let's take a taxi home.

meaning: it has been decided that; it turns out that
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことになる
usage: Presents a decision as made by others or by circumstances. People also use it for their own decisions to sound less assertive.

examples.japanese: 来年の春から、名古屋の店で働くことになりました。
examples.english: It's been decided that I'll work at the Nagoya store from next spring.

examples.japanese: 今度の日曜日、クラスのみんなでバーベキューをすることになった。
examples.english: It's been settled that the whole class will have a barbecue this Sunday.

examples.japanese: 友達の結婚式で、私がスピーチをすることになりました。
examples.english: It turns out I'll be giving a speech at my friend's wedding.

meaning: can; be able to; be possible to
structure: Verb-dict + ことができる
usage: A bit more formal than the potential form. Also used for what is possible or allowed (ここでたばこを吸うことはできません).

examples.japanese: この図書館では、本を二週間借りることができます。
examples.english: At this library, you can borrow books for two weeks.

examples.japanese: 妹はピアノを弾くことができる。
examples.english: My little sister can play the piano.

examples.japanese: ここからは富士山を見ることができません。
examples.english: You can't see Mt. Fuji from here.

meaning: can; be able to (potential form)
structure: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → e) + る / Verb-nai stem + られる (Group 2)
usage: Irregular: する → できる, 来る → 来られる. The object often takes が instead of を. In casual speech Group 2 verbs often drop ら (見れる).

examples.japanese: 私は漢字が二百ぐらい読めます。
examples.english: I can read about two hundred kanji.

examples.japanese: 兄は辛い料理が食べられない。
examples.english: My older brother can't eat spicy food.

examples.japanese: 明日のパーティーに来られますか。
examples.english: Can you come to the party tomorrow?

meaning: be done (by someone); passive voice
structure: Verb-nai stem + れる (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + られる (Group 2)
usage: Irregular: する → される, 来る → 来られる. The doer is marked with に. Often shows that the subject was troubled by someone's action (雨に降られた).

examples.japanese: 先生に作文をほめられました。
examples.english: My essay was praised by my teacher.

examples.japanese: 電車の中で足を踏まれた。
examples.english: Someone stepped on my foot on the train.

examples.japanese: この寺は六百年前に建てられました。
examples.english: This temple was built six hundred years ago.

meaning: make someone do; let someone do (causative)
structure: Verb-nai stem + せる (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + させる (Group 2)
usage: Irregular: する → させる, 来る → 来させる. With intransitive verbs the person takes を; with transitive verbs, に. Context decides 'make' or 'let'.

examples.japanese: 母は毎日弟に野菜を食べさせる。
examples.english: My mother makes my little brother eat vegetables every day.

examples.japanese: コーチは毎日、選手たちを走らせた。
examples.english: The coach made the players run every day.

examples.japanese: 息子が行きたいと言ったので、一人で旅行に行かせました。
examples.english: My son said he wanted to go, so I let him travel on his own.

meaning: be made to do (against one's will)
structure: Verb-nai stem + せられる (Group 1; short form される) / Verb-nai stem + させられる (Group 2)
usage: Irregular: する → させられる, 来る → 来させられる. The short Group 1 form (待たされる) is common in speech, but not with verbs ending in す (話させられる).

examples.japanese: 子どものころ、母に毎日ピアノを練習させられた。
examples.english: When I was a child, my mother made me practice the piano every day.

examples.japanese: 駅で三十分も待たされました。
examples.english: I was kept waiting at the station for a whole thirty minutes.

examples.japanese: 会社の飲み会で歌を歌わされた。
examples.english: I was made to sing at the company drinking party.

meaning: let's (casual); I'll (volitional form)
structure: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → o) + う / Verb-stem + よう (Group 2)
usage: Irregular: する → しよう, 来る → 来よう. The plain equivalent of 〜ましょう.

examples.japanese: 疲れたね。少し休もう。
examples.english: That was tiring, huh? Let's take a short break.

examples.japanese: 週末、一緒に映画を見ようよ。
examples.english: Let's watch a movie together this weekend.

examples.japanese: よし、今日から毎日日記を書こう。
examples.english: Right, starting today I'll write in my diary every day.

meaning: be thinking of doing; plan to
structure: Verb-volitional + と思う
usage: 〜と思う often reports a decision made just now; 〜と思っている shows a plan held for some time. Softer than つもり.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は海に行こうと思っています。
examples.english: I'm thinking of going to the beach this summer.

examples.japanese: 明日は早く起きて、公園を走ろうと思う。
examples.english: I think I'll get up early tomorrow and go for a run in the park.

examples.japanese: 新しいパソコンを買おうと思ったけど、やめました。
examples.english: I was going to buy a new computer, but I decided against it.

meaning: do it! (imperative form; blunt command)
structure: Verb-dict (Group 1: final u → e) / Verb-stem + ろ (Group 2)
usage: Irregular: する → しろ, 来る → 来い, くれる → くれ. Very blunt; heard mainly from men, on signs, in emergencies and in cheering (がんばれ).

examples.japanese: 早く起きろ！遅刻するぞ。
examples.english: Get up already! You'll be late.

examples.japanese: 危ない！止まれ！
examples.english: Look out! Stop!

examples.japanese: がんばれ！あと少しだ！
examples.english: Go for it! Just a little more!

meaning: don't! (strong prohibition)
structure: Verb-dict + な
usage: Very strong and blunt. Do not confuse it with the sentence-ending な that expresses feeling (いいな).

examples.japanese: 危ないから、この川では泳ぐな。
examples.english: It's dangerous, so don't swim in this river.

examples.japanese: もう泣くな。大丈夫だよ。
examples.english: Don't cry anymore. It's all right.

examples.japanese: 壁に「ここにごみを捨てるな」と書いてある。
examples.english: It says "Don't dump garbage here" on the wall.

meaning: do (instruction from a parent, teacher, etc.)
structure: Verb-stem + なさい
usage: Softer than the imperative form but still a firm instruction; used by parents, teachers and in exam directions, never toward superiors.

examples.japanese: もう九時よ。早く寝なさい。
examples.english: It's already nine. Go to bed now.

examples.japanese: 次の文を読んで、質問に答えなさい。
examples.english: Read the following passage and answer the questions.

examples.japanese: ご飯の前に手を洗いなさい。
examples.english: Wash your hands before eating.

meaning: if
structure: Verb-ba / i-Adj stem + ければ / na-Adj + なら / Noun + なら
usage: Focuses on the condition needed for a result. When the main clause is a request or invitation, たら is usually more natural unless the ば-clause is a state (ある, いる, adjectives).

examples.japanese: この道をまっすぐ行けば、駅に着きます。
examples.english: If you go straight along this road, you'll reach the station.

examples.japanese: 安ければ、買いたいです。
examples.english: If it's cheap, I'd like to buy it.

examples.japanese: 分からないことがあれば、いつでも聞いてください。
examples.english: If there's anything you don't understand, feel free to ask anytime.

meaning: if; when; after
structure: Verb-ta + ら / i-Adj stem + かったら / na-Adj + だったら / Noun + だったら
usage: The most versatile conditional and very common in speech. With events certain to happen it means 'when/after'.

examples.japanese: 駅に着いたら、電話してください。
examples.english: Please call me when you get to the station.

examples.japanese: もし明日雨だったら、家で映画を見よう。
examples.english: If it rains tomorrow, let's watch a movie at home.

examples.japanese: 暑かったら、窓を開けてもいいですよ。
examples.english: If you're hot, feel free to open the window.

meaning: if (it's the case that); if you're talking about
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + なら
usage: Takes up what the listener said or a situation assumed to be true, then gives advice or an opinion. Unlike たら, the main action can come before the なら-clause.

examples.japanese: 京都へ行くなら、秋がいいですよ。
examples.english: If you're going to Kyoto, autumn is a good time.

examples.japanese: パソコンのことなら、兄に聞くといいよ。
examples.english: If it's about computers, you should ask my older brother.

examples.japanese: そんなに眠いなら、今日は早く寝たら？
examples.english: If you're that sleepy, why not go to bed early today?

meaning: when; if; whenever (natural or automatic result)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai / i-Adj + と / na-Adj + だ + と / Noun + だ + と
usage: For natural results, how machines work, directions and habits. The main clause cannot be a request, wish or invitation.

examples.japanese: このボタンを押すと、お茶が出ます。
examples.english: When you press this button, tea comes out.

examples.japanese: 春になると、桜が咲きます。
examples.english: When spring comes, the cherry blossoms bloom.

examples.japanese: この道を右に曲がると、左に郵便局があります。
examples.english: If you turn right on this road, there's a post office on the left.

meaning: even if; even though
structure: Verb-te + も / i-Adj-ku + ても / na-Adj + でも / Noun + でも
usage: With question words or いくら it means 'no matter ...' (何を食べても, いくら待っても).

examples.japanese: 雨が降っても、試合はあります。
examples.english: Even if it rains, the game will go ahead.

examples.japanese: いくら練習しても、なかなか上手になりません。
examples.english: No matter how much I practice, I just don't get any better.

examples.japanese: 日曜日でも、この店は開いています。
examples.english: This shop is open even on Sundays.

meaning: although; even though (with surprise or dissatisfaction)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + のに / na-Adj + な + のに / Noun + な + のに
usage: Carries surprise, disappointment or complaint. The main clause cannot be a request or intention; use けど or ても there.

examples.japanese: 一生懸命勉強したのに、試験に落ちてしまった。
examples.english: Even though I studied really hard, I failed the exam.

examples.japanese: 日曜日なのに、会社に行かなければならない。
examples.english: Even though it's Sunday, I have to go to work.

examples.japanese: 約束したのに、彼は来なかった。
examples.english: He didn't come, even though he promised.

meaning: for; in order to (with use, time or cost)
structure: Verb-dict + のに / Noun + に
usage: Usually followed by words like 使う, いい, 便利, 必要 or かかる. With a noun, just に is used (旅行に便利).

examples.japanese: このかばんは旅行に行くのに便利です。
examples.english: This bag is handy for traveling.

examples.japanese: 家から駅まで歩くのに二十分かかります。
examples.english: It takes twenty minutes to walk from my house to the station.

examples.japanese: 引っ越しするのに十万円ぐらいかかった。
examples.english: It cost about 100,000 yen to move.

meaning: because; since
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + ので / na-Adj + な + ので / Noun + な + ので
usage: Sounds softer and more objective than から, so it is preferred when giving reasons politely or apologizing.

examples.japanese: 頭が痛いので、今日は早く帰ります。
examples.english: I have a headache, so I'm going home early today.

examples.japanese: 明日はテストなので、今夜は勉強します。
examples.english: I have a test tomorrow, so I'm studying tonight.

examples.japanese: 道がこんでいたので、少し遅れました。
examples.english: The roads were crowded, so I was a little late.

meaning: because; so (cause of a feeling or state)
structure: Verb-te / i-Adj stem + くて / na-Adj + で / Noun + で
usage: The second part is usually a feeling, a potential form or a result, not a request or intention (use から or ので for those). Negative: 〜なくて (会えなくて寂しい).

examples.japanese: ニュースを聞いて、びっくりしました。
examples.english: I was surprised to hear the news.

examples.japanese: このスープは熱くて、飲めません。
examples.english: This soup is too hot to drink.

examples.japanese: かぜで学校を休みました。
examples.english: I stayed home from school with a cold.

meaning: and what's more; and besides (listing reasons)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + し / na-Adj + だ + し / Noun + だ + し
usage: Lists several reasons or points. A single し hints that there are other reasons too.

examples.japanese: この部屋は広いし、駅から近いし、とても気に入っています。
examples.english: This apartment is spacious and close to the station, so I really like it.

examples.japanese: 今日は雨だし、疲れているし、どこにも行きたくない。
examples.english: It's raining and I'm tired, so I don't want to go anywhere today.

examples.japanese: もう遅いし、そろそろ帰ろうか。
examples.english: It's getting late, so shall we head home?

meaning: but; although; (soft lead-in)
structure: Sentence + けど / けれども
usage: More conversational than が; けれども is a little more formal than けど. Often used as a soft lead-in before a question or request.

examples.japanese: この店は高いけど、おいしい。
examples.english: This place is expensive, but the food is good.

examples.japanese: すみません、駅に行きたいんですけど、どう行けばいいですか。
examples.english: Excuse me, I'd like to get to the station. How do I get there?

examples.japanese: 何度も電話したけれども、誰も出なかった。
examples.english: I called several times, but nobody answered.

meaning: in order to; for (the sake of); because of
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-ta / Noun + の + ために
usage: For purpose, the verb must be something the subject can control (compare 〜ように). The 'because of' use sounds fairly formal.

examples.japanese: 日本の大学に入るために、毎日勉強しています。
examples.english: I study every day in order to get into a Japanese university.

examples.japanese: 家族のために、一生懸命働いている。
examples.english: I work hard for my family.

examples.japanese: 大雪のために、電車が止まりました。
examples.english: The trains stopped because of the heavy snow.

meaning: so that; in order that
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ように
usage: Used with verbs the subject can't directly control: potential forms, 分かる, 見える, negatives. For deliberate actions use ために.

examples.japanese: 後ろの人にも聞こえるように、大きな声で話してください。
examples.english: Please speak loudly so that the people in the back can hear too.

examples.japanese: 忘れないように、手にメモを書いた。
examples.english: I wrote a note on my hand so I wouldn't forget.

examples.japanese: かぜをひかないように、暖かくして寝てください。
examples.english: Keep warm when you sleep so you don't catch a cold.

meaning: try to; make sure to; make a habit of
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ようにする
usage: 〜ようにしている describes a habit you keep up. Compare 〜ようになる, a change that comes about.

examples.japanese: 毎日野菜を食べるようにしています。
examples.english: I make a point of eating vegetables every day.

examples.japanese: これからは遅刻しないようにします。
examples.english: From now on, I'll make sure not to be late.

examples.japanese: 寝る前にスマホを見ないようにしている。
examples.english: I try not to look at my phone before bed.

meaning: come to; reach the point where (change in ability or habit)
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ようになる
usage: Often used with potential verbs. For 'no longer', 〜なくなる is usually more natural than 〜ないようになる.

examples.japanese: 練習して、自転車に乗れるようになりました。
examples.english: After practicing, I became able to ride a bike.

examples.japanese: 日本に来てから、朝ご飯を食べるようになった。
examples.english: Since coming to Japan, I've started eating breakfast.

examples.japanese: 赤ちゃんが少しずつ話せるようになってきた。
examples.english: Our baby is gradually learning to talk.

meaning: want someone to do
structure: Verb-te + ほしい / Verb-nai + で + ほしい
usage: The person you want to act is marked with に. Said to a superior it can sound demanding; 〜ていただきたいです is more polite.

examples.japanese: もう少しゆっくり話してほしいです。
examples.english: I'd like you to speak a little more slowly.

examples.japanese: この話は誰にも言わないでほしい。
examples.english: I don't want you to tell anyone about this.

examples.japanese: 早く春が来てほしいなあ。
examples.english: I wish spring would hurry up and come.

meaning: (someone else) wants to
structure: Verb-stem + たがる
usage: Used for other people, since you can't directly know their wishes. Current wishes are usually expressed with 〜たがっている.

examples.japanese: 子どもたちは外で遊びたがっている。
examples.english: The children want to play outside.

examples.japanese: 弟はいつも私のゲームをやりたがる。
examples.english: My little brother always wants to play my games.

examples.japanese: 犬が散歩に行きたがっています。
examples.english: The dog wants to go for a walk.

meaning: (someone else) feels; shows signs of feeling
structure: i-Adj stem / na-Adj + がる
usage: Turns feeling adjectives (怖い, 寂しい, ほしい) into verbs describing how others seem to feel. The object of the feeling takes を.

examples.japanese: 妹は暗い所を怖がる。
examples.english: My little sister is scared of dark places.

examples.japanese: 祖母は孫に会えなくて寂しがっている。
examples.english: My grandmother is lonely because she can't see her grandchildren.

examples.japanese: 息子は新しい自転車をほしがっている。
examples.english: My son wants a new bicycle.

meaning: might; may; possibly
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かもしれない
usage: About 50% certainty or less. In casual speech it is often shortened to かも.

examples.japanese: 午後から雨が降るかもしれません。
examples.english: It might rain in the afternoon.

examples.japanese: かぎがない。電車の中で落としたかもしれない。
examples.english: My keys are gone. I might have dropped them on the train.

examples.japanese: その話は本当かもしれない。
examples.english: That story might be true.

meaning: probably; I suppose (plain form of でしょう)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + だろう
usage: Common in writing and in men's casual speech; でしょう is the polite form. Often used with たぶん or きっと, or as 〜だろうと思う.

examples.japanese: 明日はたぶん晴れるだろう。
examples.english: It will probably be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼女はもう家に着いただろう。
examples.english: She has probably gotten home by now.

examples.japanese: この問題は子どもには難しいだろうと思います。
examples.english: I think this problem is probably too hard for children.

meaning: should be; is expected to (based on reasoning)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + はずだ / na-Adj + な + はずだ / Noun + の + はずだ
usage: A confident expectation based on facts or logic, not a guess. It does not mean 'should' as a duty.

examples.japanese: 荷物は明日届くはずです。
examples.english: The package should arrive tomorrow.

examples.japanese: 彼は十年もアメリカに住んでいたから、英語が上手なはずだ。
examples.english: He lived in America for ten years, so his English should be good.

examples.japanese: おかしいな。かぎはここに置いたはずなのに。
examples.english: That's strange. I'm sure I put the keys here.

meaning: can't be; there's no way that
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + はずがない / na-Adj + な + はずがない / Noun + の + はずがない
usage: Strong denial based on reasoning. 〜ないはずだ ('should not be') is a milder expectation.

examples.japanese: あんなにまじめな人がうそをつくはずがない。
examples.english: There's no way someone that earnest would lie.

examples.japanese: 今日は日曜日だから、銀行が開いているはずがない。
examples.english: It's Sunday, so the bank can't be open.

examples.japanese: かぎはちゃんとかけたから、ドアが開いているはずがない。
examples.english: I definitely locked it, so there's no way the door is open.

meaning: it's that ...; (explaining or asking for an explanation)
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + んです / na-Adj + な + んです / Noun + な + んです
usage: Adds a sense of explaining a situation or asking for the background. Casual forms are 〜んだ and 〜の. Overusing it can sound pushy.

examples.japanese: どうしたんですか。顔色が悪いですよ。
examples.english: What's the matter? You look pale.

examples.japanese: すみません、遅れました。電車が止まっていたんです。
examples.english: Sorry I'm late. The trains had stopped.

examples.japanese: 日本語で手紙を書きたいんですが、手伝ってくれませんか。
examples.english: I want to write a letter in Japanese. Could you help me?

meaning: whether or not
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かどうか
usage: Embeds a yes-no question in a sentence. For questions with a question word, use 〜か alone (何時に来るか).

examples.japanese: 明日行けるかどうか、まだ分かりません。
examples.english: I don't know yet whether I can go tomorrow.

examples.japanese: この服が似合うかどうか、ちょっと着てみます。
examples.english: I'll try this on to see whether it suits me.

examples.japanese: そのレストランがおいしいかどうか、友達に聞いてみよう。
examples.english: I'll ask my friend whether that restaurant is any good.

meaning: embedded question (what, where, who, etc.)
structure: Question word + ... + Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + か
usage: After a noun or na-adjective, だ is dropped (誰の傘か知らない).

examples.japanese: 会議が何時に始まるか、教えてください。
examples.english: Please tell me what time the meeting starts.

examples.japanese: どこで財布をなくしたか、覚えていません。
examples.english: I don't remember where I lost my wallet.

examples.japanese: 誰が窓を割ったか、知っていますか。
examples.english: Do you know who broke the window?

meaning: I think that
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj + と思う / na-Adj + だ + と思う / Noun + だ + と思う
usage: Japanese usually negates the quoted clause (来ないと思う) rather than 思う. For another person's opinion, use 〜と思っている.

examples.japanese: この映画はきっと人気が出ると思う。
examples.english: I'm sure this movie will become popular.

examples.japanese: 彼女は今日は来ないと思います。
examples.english: I don't think she's coming today.

examples.japanese: 日本の電車はとても便利だと思います。
examples.english: I think trains in Japan are very convenient.

meaning: say that; tell (quotation)
structure: 「Sentence」 + と言う / Sentence (plain) + と言う
usage: Direct quotes go inside 「」; indirect quotes use plain forms. 〜と言っていた is common when passing on what someone said.

examples.japanese: 先生は「明日はテストがあります」と言いました。
examples.english: The teacher said, "There's a test tomorrow."

examples.japanese: 兄は今晩、帰りが遅くなると言っていた。
examples.english: My older brother said he'd be home late tonight.

examples.japanese: 日本では食べる前に「いただきます」と言います。
examples.english: In Japan, people say "itadakimasu" before eating.

meaning: only; nothing but
structure: Noun + しか + Verb-nai
usage: Always paired with a negative verb. Compared with だけ, it stresses that the amount is small or not enough.

examples.japanese: 財布に五百円しかない。
examples.english: I only have 500 yen in my wallet.

examples.japanese: このことは、あなたにしか話していません。
examples.english: I haven't told anyone but you about this.

examples.japanese: 朝はコーヒーしか飲みません。
examples.english: I only drink coffee in the morning.

meaning: nothing but; only; all
structure: Noun + ばかり
usage: Often implies there is too much of one thing. 〜てばかりいる (N3) and 〜たばかり ('just did') are separate points.

examples.japanese: 弟は肉ばかり食べて、野菜を食べない。
examples.english: My little brother eats nothing but meat and won't touch vegetables.

examples.japanese: このクラスは女の子ばかりだ。
examples.english: This class is all girls.

examples.japanese: 最近は雨の日ばかりで、洗濯ができない。
examples.english: It's been nothing but rainy days lately, so I can't do the laundry.

meaning: have just done
structure: Verb-ta + ばかり
usage: Shows the speaker feels little time has passed, even if it was weeks ago. 〜たところ refers to only moments ago.

examples.japanese: 日本に来たばかりなので、まだ日本語がよく分かりません。
examples.english: I've only just come to Japan, so I don't understand Japanese well yet.

examples.japanese: さっき昼ご飯を食べたばかりだから、おなかがいっぱいだ。
examples.english: I just had lunch, so I'm full.

examples.japanese: 買ったばかりの傘をなくしてしまった。
examples.english: I lost the umbrella I had just bought.

meaning: be about to; be in the middle of; have just done
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-te + いる / Verb-ta + ところだ
usage: Dictionary form: about to. 〜ているところ: in the middle of. 〜たところ: just finished. It pinpoints the stage of an action.

examples.japanese: 今から出かけるところです。
examples.english: I'm just about to go out.

examples.japanese: 今、晩ご飯を作っているところだから、後で電話するね。
examples.english: I'm in the middle of making dinner, so I'll call you later.

examples.japanese: ちょうど今、駅に着いたところです。
examples.english: I've just this moment arrived at the station.

meaning: easy to; hard to
structure: Verb-stem + やすい / Verb-stem + にくい
usage: Both conjugate like i-adjectives. やすい can also mean 'tends to' (この服は汚れやすい).

examples.japanese: このペンは書きやすいです。
examples.english: This pen is easy to write with.

examples.japanese: 先生の説明は分かりやすい。
examples.english: The teacher's explanations are easy to understand.

examples.japanese: この魚は骨が多くて食べにくい。
examples.english: This fish has a lot of bones, so it's hard to eat.

meaning: start doing; finish doing; keep doing
structure: Verb-stem + 始める / Verb-stem + 終わる / Verb-stem + 続ける
usage: 〜終わる is used with actions that have a clear end (読む, 食べる, 書く). 〜終える is a more formal alternative.

examples.japanese: 去年からギターを習い始めました。
examples.english: I started learning guitar last year.

examples.japanese: その本、読み終わったら貸してくれない？
examples.english: When you finish reading that book, could you lend it to me?

examples.japanese: 三時間も歩き続けて、足が痛くなった。
examples.english: My feet started to hurt after walking for three hours straight.

meaning: suddenly start doing; burst out
structure: Verb-stem + 出す
usage: Implies a sudden, often uncontrolled start. Unlike 〜始める, it is not used for planned actions or in requests.

examples.japanese: 赤ちゃんが急に泣き出した。
examples.english: The baby suddenly burst out crying.

examples.japanese: さっきまで晴れていたのに、急に雨が降り出した。
examples.english: It was sunny until a moment ago, but suddenly it started to rain.

meaning: not as ... as
structure: Noun / Verb-plain + ほど + i-Adj-ku + ない / na-Adj + ではない
usage: The item before ほど is the standard of comparison. Always followed by a negative.

examples.japanese: 今年の夏は去年ほど暑くない。
examples.english: This summer isn't as hot as last year.

examples.japanese: 私の町は東京ほどにぎやかではありません。
examples.english: My town isn't as lively as Tokyo.

examples.japanese: テストは思ったほど難しくなかった。
examples.english: The test wasn't as hard as I'd expected.

meaning: not easily; just won't; not readily
structure: なかなか + Verb-nai
usage: Shows that something doesn't happen as quickly or easily as hoped. With a positive form, なかなか means 'quite' (なかなかおいしい).

examples.japanese: バスがなかなか来ない。
examples.english: The bus just isn't coming.

examples.japanese: 漢字がなかなか覚えられません。
examples.english: I just can't seem to memorize kanji.

examples.japanese: 子どもがなかなか寝てくれない。
examples.english: The kids just won't go to sleep.

meaning: each; at a time; little by little
structure: Noun (quantity) + ずつ

examples.japanese: りんごを一人に二つずつ配った。
examples.english: I handed out two apples to each person.

examples.japanese: 毎日少しずつ漢字を覚えています。
examples.english: I'm learning kanji a little at a time every day.

examples.japanese: 一人ずつ部屋に入ってください。
examples.english: Please enter the room one at a time.

meaning: as many as; as much as; (with a negative) not even one
structure: Noun (number + counter) + も
usage: Shows the speaker feels the amount is large. With 一 + counter and a negative verb, it means 'not even one'.

examples.japanese: 昨日は十時間も寝てしまった。
examples.english: I slept for a whole ten hours yesterday.

examples.japanese: このかばんは五万円もするんですか。
examples.english: This bag costs as much as 50,000 yen?

examples.japanese: 財布の中に一円もない。
examples.english: I don't have a single yen in my wallet.

meaning: by (a deadline); before
structure: Noun / Verb-dict + までに
usage: までに marks a deadline for a one-time action; まで marks how long something continues (六時まで働く).

examples.japanese: レポートは金曜日までに出してください。
examples.english: Please hand in the report by Friday.

examples.japanese: 六時までに家に帰らなければならない。
examples.english: I have to be home by six.

examples.japanese: 暗くなるまでに山を下りよう。
examples.english: Let's get down the mountain before it gets dark.

meaning: sometimes; there are times when
structure: Verb-dict / Verb-nai + ことがある
usage: Takes the dictionary or ない form. With the past form (〜たことがある) it means 'have done before' instead.

examples.japanese: 忙しいときは、朝ご飯を食べないことがあります。
examples.english: When I'm busy, I sometimes skip breakfast.

examples.japanese: この道は冬になると、雪で通れなくなることがある。
examples.english: In winter, this road sometimes becomes impassable because of snow.

examples.japanese: 週末は家族で料理をすることがある。
examples.english: On weekends, my family sometimes cooks together.

meaning: have to; must (conversational)
structure: Verb-nai + といけない / Verb-nai stem + なくちゃ
usage: Everyday alternatives to なければならない. なくちゃ comes from なくては; なきゃ (from なければ) is also very common.

examples.japanese: 明日は早いから、もう寝ないといけない。
examples.english: I have an early start tomorrow, so I need to go to bed now.

examples.japanese: あ、もうこんな時間！帰らなくちゃ。
examples.english: Oh, look at the time! I have to go home.

examples.japanese: この薬は毎日飲まないといけません。
examples.english: You have to take this medicine every day.

meaning: please let me (do)
structure: Verb-nai stem + せてください (Group 1) / Verb-nai stem + させてください (Group 2)
usage: Built on the causative て-form (する → させて). 〜させていただけませんか is more polite.

examples.japanese: 少し考えさせてください。
examples.english: Please let me think about it for a bit.

examples.japanese: 今日は私に払わせてください。
examples.english: Please let me pay today.

examples.japanese: 体の調子が悪いので、今日は早く帰らせてください。
examples.english: I'm not feeling well, so please let me go home early today.

meaning: honorific verbs; respectful language for others' actions
structure: いらっしゃる（行く・来る・いる） / 召し上がる（食べる・飲む） / おっしゃる（言う） / なさる（する） / ご覧になる（見る） / くださる（くれる）
usage: Raises the actions of people you respect, such as customers, teachers and superiors. Never use it for your own actions.

examples.japanese: 社長は何時ごろいらっしゃいますか。
examples.english: Around what time will the company president be here?

examples.japanese: 先生、どうぞ召し上がってください。
examples.english: Please help yourself, sensei.

examples.japanese: 部長は会議でそうおっしゃいました。
examples.english: The department manager said so at the meeting.

meaning: humble verbs; modest language for one's own actions
structure: 参る（行く・来る） / おる（いる） / いただく（食べる・飲む・もらう） / 申す（言う） / いたす（する） / 拝見する（見る） / 伺う（聞く・訪ねる）
usage: Lowers your own actions, or your group's, toward someone you respect. 参る, おる, 申す and いたす also make speech sound formal in general.

examples.japanese: 明日の午後、そちらに伺います。
examples.english: I'll come to your office tomorrow afternoon.

examples.japanese: 初めまして。リンと申します。
examples.english: Nice to meet you. My name is Lin.

examples.japanese: お手紙、拝見しました。
examples.english: I have read your letter.

meaning: (honorific) someone respected does
structure: お + Verb-stem + になる
usage: Not used with one-syllable stems (見る, 寝る) or verbs that have special forms (行く → いらっしゃる). する-nouns take ご + Noun + になる (ご利用になる).

examples.japanese: 先生はもうお帰りになりました。
examples.english: The teacher has already gone home.

examples.japanese: この本をお読みになりましたか。
examples.english: Have you read this book?

examples.japanese: 社長はいつもこのホテルにお泊まりになります。
examples.english: The company president always stays at this hotel.

meaning: (humble) I do (for someone respected)
structure: お + Verb-stem + する / ご + Noun + する
usage: Only for actions that affect or benefit the other person. お〜いたします is even more formal.

examples.japanese: 重そうですね。お持ちしましょうか。
examples.english: That looks heavy. Shall I carry it for you?

examples.japanese: 後で詳しくご説明します。
examples.english: I'll explain in detail later.

examples.japanese: 駅までお送りします。
examples.english: I'll see you to the station.

meaning: is; am; are (very polite copula)
structure: Noun / na-Adj + でございます
usage: The very polite version of です, typical of shop and hotel staff speaking to customers. ございます on its own is the polite form of あります.

examples.japanese: お手洗いはあちらでございます。
examples.english: The restroom is over there.

examples.japanese: こちらが、お部屋のかぎでございます。
examples.english: Here is your room key.

examples.japanese: はい、山田商店でございます。
examples.english: Hello, Yamada Shoten speaking.

meaning: don't mind if; it's fine if
structure: Verb-te + も構わない / i-Adj-ku + ても構わない / na-Adj + でも構わない / Noun + でも構わない
usage: A little more formal than 〜てもいい. 〜なくても構わない means 'it's fine not to'.

examples.japanese: ここに荷物を置いても構いませんか。
examples.english: Do you mind if I leave my bags here?

examples.japanese: 少しぐらい高くても構わないから、いい辞書を買いたい。
examples.english: I don't mind if it's a bit pricey; I want to buy a good dictionary.

examples.japanese: 返事は明日でも構いませんよ。
examples.english: It's fine if you answer tomorrow.

meaning: the act of doing (turns a verb phrase into a noun)
structure: Verb-plain + の / Verb-plain + こと
usage: の is preferred with perception verbs (見る, 聞こえる) and in casual speech; こと is needed before です/だ and in set patterns such as 〜ことができる.

examples.japanese: 私は写真を撮るのが好きです。
examples.english: I like taking photos.

examples.japanese: 趣味は古い映画を見ることです。
examples.english: My hobby is watching old movies.

examples.japanese: かぎをかけるのを忘れました。
examples.english: I forgot to lock the door.

meaning: should have (done); I wish I had
structure: Verb-ba + よかった / Verb-nai stem + なければよかった
usage: Expresses regret about the past. 〜たらよかった is a common conversational alternative.

examples.japanese: もっと早く家を出ればよかった。
examples.english: I should have left home earlier.

examples.japanese: あんなこと、言わなければよかった。
examples.english: I wish I hadn't said that.

examples.japanese: 傘を持ってくればよかったなあ。
examples.english: I wish I'd brought an umbrella.

meaning: why don't you ...?; how about ...?
structure: Verb-ta + らどう
usage: Often shortened to 〜たら？. Can sound pushy toward superiors; 〜たらいかがですか is the polite version.

examples.japanese: 疲れているなら、少し休んだらどう？
examples.english: If you're tired, why not rest a bit?

examples.japanese: 分からなければ、先生に聞いてみたらどうですか。
examples.english: If you don't understand, why don't you try asking the teacher?

meaning: had better; should
structure: Verb-ta / Verb-nai + ほうがいい
usage: For advice, the past form (行ったほうがいい) is the usual choice and sounds stronger. The negative uses the ない form, not the past.

examples.japanese: 熱があるなら、病院に行ったほうがいいですよ。
examples.english: If you have a fever, you'd better go to the hospital.

examples.japanese: 夜遅くに一人で歩かないほうがいい。
examples.english: You'd better not walk alone late at night.

examples.japanese: 大事な書類は、コピーしておいたほうがいいですよ。
examples.english: It's a good idea to make copies of important documents.

meaning: things like A and B; A, B and so on (casual)
structure: Noun + とか + Noun + とか / Verb-dict + とか + Verb-dict + とか
usage: More casual than 〜や〜など, and it can also list verbs or whole phrases.

examples.japanese: 冷蔵庫に卵とか牛乳とかが入っています。
examples.english: There are things like eggs and milk in the fridge.

examples.japanese: 休みの日は、映画とか買い物とかに行きます。
examples.english: On my days off, I go to the movies, go shopping, that kind of thing.

examples.japanese: 健康のために、野菜を食べるとか運動するとか、何かしたほうがいい。
examples.english: For your health, you should do something, like eating vegetables or exercising.

meaning: etc.; and so on; such as
structure: Noun + など
usage: Often paired with や (AやBなど). After a single noun it softens a suggestion.

examples.japanese: 机の上に本やノートなどがあります。
examples.english: On the desk there are books, notebooks and so on.

examples.japanese: 夏休みに京都や奈良などに行きました。
examples.english: During summer vacation I went to places like Kyoto and Nara.

examples.japanese: お茶など、いかがですか。
examples.english: Would you care for some tea or something?

meaning: or something (softening a suggestion)
structure: Noun + でも
usage: Offers one example while leaving other options open, which makes invitations and advice sound less pushy.

examples.japanese: ちょっと休んで、コーヒーでも飲みませんか。
examples.english: Why don't we take a break and have a coffee or something?

examples.japanese: 雨だから、家でゲームでもしよう。
examples.english: It's raining, so let's play a game or something at home.

examples.japanese: 暇なら、本でも読んだら？
examples.english: If you're bored, why not read a book or something?

meaning: -ness (turns an adjective into a noun of degree)
structure: i-Adj stem + さ / na-Adj + さ
usage: いい becomes よさ. Common for measurements (高さ, 重さ, 大きさ, 長さ).

examples.japanese: この橋の長さはどのくらいですか。
examples.english: How long is this bridge?

examples.japanese: 山の上の寒さにびっくりした。
examples.english: I was surprised by how cold it was at the top of the mountain.

examples.japanese: この仕事の大変さは、やってみないと分からない。
examples.english: You can't understand how tough this job is until you try it.

meaning: -th (ordinal: first, second, third ...)
structure: Noun (number + counter) + 目

examples.japanese: 右から三つ目の建物が図書館です。
examples.english: The third building from the right is the library.

examples.japanese: 日本に来るのは今回で二回目です。
examples.english: This is my second time coming to Japan.

examples.japanese: 二つ目の角を左に曲がってください。
examples.english: Please turn left at the second corner.

meaning: every other; at intervals of
structure: Noun (number + counter) + おきに
usage: With days (一日おき) it skips one unit, meaning 'every other day'. With minutes or distances it usually just means 'every X'.

examples.japanese: このバスは十五分おきに来ます。
examples.english: This bus comes every fifteen minutes.

examples.japanese: 一日おきにジョギングをしています。
examples.english: I go jogging every other day.

examples.japanese: 道の両側に、木が五メートルおきに植えてある。
examples.english: Trees are planted every five meters on both sides of the road.

meaning: make (something) ...; change something to a state
structure: i-Adj-ku + する / na-Adj + に + する / Noun + に + する
usage: Someone deliberately changes something. Compare 〜くなる / 〜になる, where the change happens by itself.

examples.japanese: テレビの音を小さくしてください。
examples.english: Please turn the TV down.

examples.japanese: お客さんが来るから、部屋をきれいにしよう。
examples.english: We have guests coming, so let's tidy up the room.

examples.japanese: 暑いので、髪を短くしました。
examples.english: It's hot, so I had my hair cut short.

meaning: (a smell, sound, taste or feeling) is perceived
structure: Noun + がする
usage: Used with におい, 音, 声, 味 and 気 (〜気がする: 'have a feeling that').

examples.japanese: 台所からいいにおいがする。
examples.english: There's a nice smell coming from the kitchen.

examples.japanese: 外で変な音がしました。
examples.english: I heard a strange noise outside.

examples.japanese: このお茶は少し甘い味がする。
examples.english: This tea tastes slightly sweet.

meaning: I wonder
structure: Verb-plain / i-Adj / na-Adj / Noun + かな / かしら
usage: A soft question, often said to oneself. かしら sounds feminine and a little old-fashioned. 〜ないかな can express a wish (早く来ないかな).

examples.japanese: 明日は晴れるかな。
examples.english: I wonder if it'll be sunny tomorrow.

examples.japanese: このお菓子、誰が買ってきたのかな。
examples.english: I wonder who bought these snacks.

examples.japanese: この服、私に似合うかしら。
examples.english: I wonder if this outfit suits me.

pattern: 〜てくれませんか / 〜ていただけませんか
meaning: could you please ...? (polite request)
structure: Verb-te + くれませんか / Verb-te + いただけませんか
usage: Softer than 〜てください. Politeness rises from 〜てくれませんか to 〜てもらえませんか to 〜ていただけませんか.

examples.japanese: すみません、写真を撮ってくれませんか。
examples.english: Excuse me, could you take my picture?

examples.japanese: この書類の書き方を教えていただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you please show me how to fill out this form?

examples.japanese: もう少し大きい声で話していただけませんか。
examples.english: Could you speak a little louder, please?

meaning: without doing; instead of doing
structure: Verb-nai + で
usage: 〜ずに (N3) means the same but is more formal. Differs from 〜なくて, which gives a reason.

examples.japanese: 今朝は朝ご飯を食べないで学校に行った。
examples.english: This morning I went to school without eating breakfast.

examples.japanese: 傘を持たないで出かけて、雨にぬれてしまった。
examples.english: I went out without an umbrella and got soaked.

examples.japanese: エレベーターを使わないで、階段で上がりましょう。
examples.english: Let's take the stairs instead of the elevator.
